modules.name: shared-types
owns: Cross-module enums: LeaveType, LeaveStatus, NotificationType, AuditAction, EntityType
Shared value types / DTOs used by more than one module (e.g. LeaveRequestSummary, BalanceSnapshot)
index.ts barrel re-exporting all shared types

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Shared foundations (types + unit of work)
recommended_phases.rationale: No module can compile without shared enums and the transaction boundary. Establish src/shared/types/ (leave.types.ts + index.ts barrel) and src/shared/db/ IUnitOfWork + implementation. Resolves the LeaveStatus enum conflict (adopt PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED per root ARCHITECTURE.md).

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Leaf modules: employee, policy, audit
recommended_phases.rationale: These modules depend only on shared-types and shared-db (no cross-module service deps), so they are the innermost domain modules and must exist before anything consumes them. Each ships model + repository + service + routes + index.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — balance and notification
recommended_phases.rationale: balance depends on audit (for balance mutations) and shared foundations; notification depends only on shared foundations. Both are prerequisites for leave's transaction orchestration.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — leave orchestration module
recommended_phases.rationale: leave is the outermost domain module: it composes balance, notification, audit, employee, and policy inside a single IUnitOfWork transaction for create/approve/reject/cancel. Build last so all its dependencies exist.

app_notes: Application slice for the leave management module. Layering: presentation (routes) → application (services) → domain (entities/repositories) → infrastructure (shared-db). Dependencies flow inward; leave is the outermost domain module composing balance, notification, audit, employee, and policy inside a single IUnitOfWork transaction. Cross-module enums (LeaveType, LeaveStatus, NotificationType, AuditAction, EntityType) live in src/shared/types/ per the shared-value-type rule. Transaction boundary: services own the unit of work; shared-db's IUnitOfWork.withTransaction opens BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK; participating repo/service methods take an optional client as the last parameter. Verified dependencyMap is acyclic (leave → {balance, notification, audit, employee, policy, shared-types, shared-db}; balance → {audit, shared-types, shared-db}; all others → {shared-types, shared-db} only).

open_questions.question: Which LeaveStatus enum values are authoritative — DOMAIN.md (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED) or root ARCHITECTURE.md (PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED)?
open_questions.impact: Affects the shared-types enum definition, leave lifecycle state-transition rules, and any existing migration/seed data. Must be settled before Phase 1.
candidate_options: Support both via a superset with a migration mapping

open_questions.impact: Determines whether the application slice is built from scratch or recovered from an external source; affects sequencing and effort estimates.
candidate_options: Re-implement phases 1-6 from scratch per this design
Locate an external source/branch containing the missing files

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole } populated by a JWT bearer auth middleware (Fastify preHandler) that verifies the token and attaches identity. UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. RBAC enforced by a route-level requireRole(...) guard, never inline: create/cancel leave → employee (own resource); approve/reject → manager or hr_admin; balance/policy/audit reads → employee (own) or hr_admin.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (code VALIDATION_ERROR); authentication failure → 401 (code UNAUTHORIZED); authorization failure → 403 (code FORBIDDEN); not found → 404 (code NOT_FOUND). All async errors caught and mapped (GP-006); no unhandled rejections.
